chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Haruriyyah (Khawarij) were mentioned before Ali (peace be upon him). He said: 'If they rise up against a just Imam or a group, fight them. And if they rise up against a biased/unjust Imam, do not fight them, for they have a valid argument in that.'

key_terms.اَلْحَرُورِيَّةُ: The Haruriyyah, referring to the Khawarij sect

ai.seo_question: When should the Khawarij be fought according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of contextualizing rebellion (*bagh*) based on the ruler's justice, a key distinction from the Sunni view which often treats all rebels as a single entity. Imam Ali (AS) advises fighting the Khawarij only when they oppose a just Imam, but sparing them when they rise against an unjust ruler, as their grievance holds valid merit (*maqalan*). This underscores the dynamic nature of political legitimacy in Shia thought, where the ruler's moral standing directly influences the status of the rebels.
